questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that stop them quickly.
They turn more easily than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than other vehicles going the same speed. A passenger vehicle going 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck going 55 mph needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: Which habit is dangerous in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely
Not watching carefully for workers and equipment
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down for traffic and keep safe distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and equipment.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for vehicles with disability license plates, disabled veteran plates, or disabled parking permits.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road
Loose gravel
Slippery when wet

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Drive carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. You should drive:

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
Only one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in the mirrors. The truck driver will not know you are there. Following too close is dangerous because you have no safety space if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that you are leaving a divided one-way highway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have big blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Even with good mirrors, blind spots exist that mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check these areas.

questions.question: When pulling into traffic from a curb, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a gap large enough to speed up to traffic speed.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough to speed up to traffic speed.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to reach the speed of other traffic.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes or unusual events causes traffic congestion. Avoid this habit.

questions.question: As your speed increases, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look ahead down the road.
Change lanes frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead down the road.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster, your vehicle takes longer to stop. Looking ahead gives you time to see hazards and react safely.

questions.question: When passing another car, you have enough space to return to your lane when:

options.text: The other driver signals for you to move back.
You look over your shoulder and see the car behind you.
You can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Seeing both headlights in your mirror means you have enough safe space between your vehicle and the other car. Then you can return to your lane.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and hazmat trucks.
Watch for trains coming from both directions.
Do both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both A and B.
questions.explanation: Be very careful at all railroad crossings. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Also watch for vehicles like school buses and hazmat trucks, which must stop at all crossings.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol can affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and coordination.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol can harm your judgment and physical control. Any alcohol can make it unsafe to drive.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means you:

options.text: May turn in that direction after slowing down and checking traffic.
Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
May turn in that direction after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must wait until a green light or green arrow appears before turning.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Dangerous only in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always risky because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Always use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe for driving if you take the recommended dose.
Any medicine prescribed by a doctor is safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and affect your driving. Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can be dangerous. Always check how your medicine affects you before driving.

questions.question: With a Class C driver license, you may operate:

options.text: Any motor vehicle, regardless of size or weight.
A vehicle weighing less than 26,001 pounds.
A vehicle weighing more than 26,001 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle weighing less than 26,001 pounds.
questions.explanation: A Class C license allows you to drive vehicles that weigh less than 26,001 pounds.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming cars.
Stay farther behind the car ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between your car and the car ahead when driving at night. It is harder to see, so you need more time to stop. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights as they can blind you.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Release the gas pedal first. This creates space between you and the other car without causing you to slam on the brakes or swerve.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can drive completely across before the light turns red. Even if the light is green, blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: You are already in an intersection when the green light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Keep moving and safely clear the intersection.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep moving and safely clear the intersection.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, drive through quickly and safely to clear the intersection.

questions.question: An oncoming car has its high beams on and you cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving on the highway helps you:

options.text: Keep up with traffic speed.
Avoid sudden braking or turning.
See police officers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Looking far ahead helps you see problems early and react smoothly. This lets you avoid sudden stops, change lanes safely, save fuel, and keep traffic moving steadily.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle on the road ahead?

options.text: Keep your speed and drive through the water.
Avoid it if you can.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles, ice, wet leaves, and oil. The safest surface to drive on is dry and solid.
